BOOKER GAINOR.background: Democrat born in Cairo, Georgia; Cairo High School 2007 and B.S. in business administration (marketing) from Florida A&M University, 2012. his 2020 survey says he worked as a cable technician for Community Network Services after college. WENDELL WILLARD.name: Wendell Willard
WENDELL WILLARD.background: Republican attorney from Sandy Springs; born in Decatur and raised in DeKalb County (age 72 in March 2013). Law degree, Atlanta Law School (1965). Active in Republican politics since working on Richard Nixon's 1960 campaign; lost a 1970 legislative bid; moved to north Fulton in 1986. Elected to the Georgia House in 2000 (served from 2001), representing District 51 (Sandy Springs panhandle and parts of Johns Creek and Roswell); chaired the House Judiciary Committee from 2005 and served on Appropriations, Ethics, Rules and Ways and Means. Helped write the charter of the City of Sandy Springs (incorporated 2005) and served as its city attorney; runs a private law practice. Married to Vicki. Announced in June 2016 that his 2017-18 term would be his last. Official results: unopposed in the May 24, 2016 State House District 51 (Republican primary) (1,526 votes); unopposed in the Nov. 8, 2016 State House District 51 (19,210 votes).
WENDELL WILLARD.ideology: Calls himself a "Theodore Roosevelt Republican," fiscally conservative and socially progressive (Rough Draft Atlanta / Reporter Newspapers, 2013). The same profile described him as a quiet, measured and influential legislator.
WENDELL WILLARD.record: Chairman of the House Judiciary Committee from 2005. Legislative work cited by Gov. Deal's office: the 2004 Child Protection Law, the 2005 creation of Sandy Springs and later Johns Creek and Milton, the 2006 eminent domain law, the 2011 rewrite of the Georgia Evidence Code, and sponsorship of the 2013 Juvenile Justice Reform Act. Honors listed there include the State Bar of Georgia's Lifetime Achievement Award (2013), the Big Voice for Children Award, two Georgia Council on Aging Legislator Awards and the Georgia Municipal Association's "Champion of Georgia's Cities." In 2016 he said he would make no endorsement in the 2018 open-seat race.
WENDELL WILLARD.notes: Rechecked 2026-11-05. Start year: Deal's page says first elected 2001; the 2013 profile says he won the seat in 2000 (took office 2001). In 2016 he said his last term would bring his service to 18 years, which does not match a 2001 start; treat as 2001-2019. State roll calls left to the General Assembly feed.

positions.stance: Led the 2013 juvenile justice overhaul to treat truants differently from dangerous young offenders, calling a 65% recidivism rate unacceptable: "We're really, as a state, damaging the greatest asset that we've got."
Co-signed House Bill 427 to protect LGBT state employees from workplace discrimination.
Described himself as a "guardian" in the legislature for bills affecting Sandy Springs and other cities.

statements.text: Said he was ready for "fresh ideas" in the seat and would retire in 2018 at the end of his next term.
"You're going to be known for how you conduct yourself."

WRIGHT BARKSDALE.name: T. Wright Barksdale
WRIGHT BARKSDALE.background: T. Wright Barksdale III, a Washington County native who lives in Jones County with his wife and three children (age 36 in March 2024). Graduated summa cum laude from Georgia Southern University (2009) and earned his law degree from John Marshall Law School in Atlanta (2012). Spent seven years as an assistant district attorney in the Ocmulgee Judicial Circuit under the late DA Fred Bright; elected Ocmulgee Circuit District Attorney in 2020, succeeding Stephen A. Bradley (elected a superior court judge), and re-elected unopposed in 2024. The eight-county circuit covers Baldwin, Putnam, Jones, Morgan, Greene, Hancock, Wilkinson and Jasper counties. Presiding member of the Prosecuting Attorneys Qualifications Commission; council member of the Prosecuting Attorneys' Council of Georgia and vice president of the District Attorneys' Association of Georgia.
WRIGHT BARKSDALE.record: Won the 2020 Republican primary for Ocmulgee Circuit DA with 81.7% (over Carl Cansino) and was unopposed in the 2020 general and in 2024. By March 2024 his office had tried 38 homicide cases in the circuit and worked through a COVID-19 case backlog, trying serious violent cases in gymnasiums and civic halls. He was lead prosecutor in two death penalty trials over the murders of corrections Sgts. Christopher Monica and Curtis Billue during a prison escape, and still tries murders and other violent felonies personally.
WRIGHT BARKSDALE.notes: Full name T. Wright Barksdale III. Branch says he had no campaign website and did not answer its questionnaire (April 2024). Branch quote on 38 homicide trials is undated there; Union-Recorder dates it March 2024.

positions.stance: Says his office's record is 'very effective, efficient and successful' and compares favorably with any prosecutor in Georgia; priorities are building on the foundation of predecessors Fred Bright and Stephen Bradley, pursuing several major trials, treating people fairly and protecting schools, families and community life.

statements.text: "I am deeply honored to serve the people of this circuit as their district attorney."
"I do this because I truly love each and every one of our communities within this circuit."

ZAINE HEDGE.name: Zaine D. Hedge
ZAINE HEDGE.background: Lithia Springs attorney. B.A. English and literature, Reinhardt University; J.D. Charleston School of Law. Former partner at Hedge Law Office, LLC in Douglasville (personal injury, criminal defense); lecturer at Kennesaw State University; attorney with Georgia's Juvenile Court Administrative Council (per Branch). Appointed chief magistrate of Douglas County in 2026, then elected to the post on May 19, 2026. Board member of the Good Samaritan Center; youth leader at Crossroads Church.
ZAINE HEDGE.record: Finished third (22.9%) in the May 21, 2024 race for the open Douglas Circuit Superior Court seat of Chief Judge William 'Beau' McClain. Appointed Douglas County chief magistrate in 2026 and won the May 19, 2026 election for the office with 63.7% over Dondell R. Patterson.
ZAINE HEDGE.notes: Branch shows 17,812 votes for Hedge; use SOS. Branch lists no stated positions or endorsements.
